summary: The note describes how local retailers in the community are adopting e-commerce and digital marketing as of late 2023, treating the shift as necessary for survival and growth. It covers online stores, content marketing, social media, SEO, analytics, email marketing, digital skills training and partnerships, illustrated with local business owners and experts. Examples report sales gains, follower growth and increased repeat customers.
one_line: Local retailers in late 2023 are embracing e-commerce, content, social media, SEO, analytics and email marketing to survive and grow.
key_facts: Mary Johnson, owner of a local boutique, says sales increased by 30% since her website launched on September 15th, 2023.
Shopify, WooCommerce, and Magento are the platforms commonly mentioned for local retailers setting up and managing online stores.
A Local Retail Association study dated September 2023 found about 80% of consumers research products online before purchasing, in-store or online.
Digital marketing expert Alex Kim says a business's digital footprint is often a customer's first interaction with a brand, and a poor or absent online presence can send them to a competitor.
Sarah and Tom Fletcher's local hardware store launched a YouTube channel in early September 2023 with DIY home improvement video tutorials, boosting in-store visits.
Joseph Bentley, a local coffee shop owner, used Instagram daily posts and stories, and his follower count crossed 10,000 as of November 2023.
Local SEO tactics include targeting local keywords, managing Google My Business listings, and collecting positive reviews.
SEO specialist Emma Wallace says some clients doubled their online traffic in just a few months since September 2023 by focusing on local SEO.
Data analyst Neil Gupta said in a webinar on October 20, 2023 that harnessing data analytics is 'no longer a luxury—it's a must for staying competitive.'
Carolina Remirez started an email campaign for her bookstore in September 2023 and reports a 25% increase in recurring customers since starting a monthly newsletter.
Retail consultant Henry Choi says tools are useless without the right skills; businesses are enrolling employees in digital skills workshops and working with digital marketing agencies.
Local retailers are forming partnerships with local influencers, other businesses for cross-promotion, and technology providers.
